SMTO-GML-0038 — Gmail had a problem on Google's side

GUID: a1cadaf2-3f0e-4de5-bae2-58d99b9c100b
Slug: gmail-provider-service-unavailable
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Google's Gmail service had an internal problem while handling the request. If the Task was sending or changing email, that change may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail in your browser. If it's slow or showing errors, wait until it works normally again. The problem is on Google's side, so SMTO can't get past it until Gmail recovers.
  2. If the Task was sending or changing email, check Sent, Drafts or Trash in Gmail to see whether it already happened. Google may have completed the change before it failed to answer SMTO.
  3. Once Gmail works, ask SMTO again in the conversation, only for what is still missing. Asking only for missing work avoids sending the same email twice.

What success looks like

  • Gmail loads normally, SMTO completes the request, and each email or change appears only once.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking again. If Gmail works in your browser but SMTO keeps getting this error, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't set up repeated retries, and don't resend anything until you've checked the Sent folder.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned an HTTP 5xx server error for a Gmail request.

What this means

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status at least 500 and chooses the provider-service-failure category. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status at least 500 and chooses the provider-service-failure category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect service availability and original write evidence; a server error alone does not prove no mutation occurred.

How to fix it

  • Gmail reads already retry 500, 502, 503 and 504 responses up to three attempts. Check Google Workspace service status and wait for recovery; for any write, inspect the live mailbox (Sent, Drafts, labels, Trash) of the same account and resubmit only work confirmed missing. Avoid tight retry loops and never replay an uncertain write.
  • Inspect provider availability and the current resource state. Wait for service recovery before another read; reconcile writes through authoritative state before repeating them.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Availability recovers and any uncertain original effect is reconciled before another write.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
